facts.statement: Tendaguria was estimated to be twenty meters (sixty-six feet) in length.
facts.quote: Its length is estimated at twenty meters (sixty-six feet).

facts.statement: Tendaguria is distinguished from other sauropods by having two distinct cavities on the diapophyses of its anterior dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: It can be distinguished from other sauropods by the presence of two distinct cavities on the diapophyses of the anterior dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Tendaguria is unique among turiasaurs for having a defined ridge in the middle of its anteriormost dorsal spines.
facts.quote: Additionally, it is unique from other turiasaurs in that it has a defined ridge in the middle of the anteriormost dorsal spines.

facts.statement: German geologist Wilhelm Bornhardt discovered two sauropod vertebrae near Nambango in 1911, fifteen kilometers southeast of Tendaguru Hill.
facts.quote: In 1911, German geologist Wilhelm Bornhardt at Nambango in German East Africa discovered two sauropod vertebrae, fifteen kilometers (nine miles) southeast of Tendaguru Hill.

facts.statement: Werner Janensch described the initial finds in 1929 but did not name them at that time.
facts.quote: These were described by Werner Janensch in 1929, but not named.

facts.statement: The genus was formally named by José Fernando Bonaparte, Wolf-Dieter Heinrich, and Rupert Wild in 2000.
facts.quote: The finds were formally named by José Fernando Bonaparte, Wolf-Dieter Heinrich and Rupert Wild in 2000.

facts.statement: The type specimen consists of two anterior dorsal vertebrae found in the Upper Saurian Bed dating to the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: The type specimen consists of two syntypes, MB.R.2092.1 (NB4) and MB.R.2092.2 (NB5), probably uncovered in the Upper Saurian Bed (Obere Dinosauriermergel), Tendaguru Series, dating from the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: The specimen was found in Tanzania, 15 kilometers from Tendaguru Hill, likely in the Upper Saurian Bed of the Tendaguru Formation.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue encontrado en Tanzania, a 15 kilómetros de la colina Tendaguru probablemente en el Lecho Sauriano Superior, Formación Tendaguru, Jurásico Superior.

facts.statement: Mannion et al. initially placed Tendaguria in Eusauropoda in 2013, but later assigned it to Turiasauria in 2019.
facts.quote: Mannion et al. en 2013 los colocarón en Eusauropoda y en 2019 lo asignaron a Turiasauria basándose en la anatomía comparada y un análisis filogenético donde se recupera como el taxón hermano de Moabosaurus dentro de este último clado.

facts.statement: Due to its unique morphology, Tendaguria was originally classified as Sauropoda incertae sedis, with authors even creating a separate family, Tendaguriidae.
facts.quote: Due to its unique morphology, Tendaguria defied classification in the original description, where the authors placed it as Sauropoda incertae sedis, though also naming a separate Tendaguriidae.

facts.statement: Tendaguria is a highly derived sauropod in which the axial musculature has likely shifted position to the dorsal surface of the transverse processes.
facts.quote: Tendaguria es un saurópodo altamente derivado, en el que la musculatura axial ha cambiado de posición probablemente a la superficie dorsal de los procesos transversales

facts.statement: The time range for Tendaguria is the Tithonian stage, from 149.2 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 143.1 million years ago)
